text: What actually happens to your coffee after you drink it?
Caffeine makes it release more acid.
Then your small intestine absorbs most of the caffeine.
Almost all of it is absorbed within about forty-five minutes.
It reaches your liver first, through the hepatic portal vein.
Most of it passes right through.
Your blood carries it to your heart, then up to your brain.
There it blocks adenosine, which builds sleep pressure.
Blood levels peak anywhere from fifteen minutes to two hours.
Over the next hours, your liver breaks it down with C Y P one A two.
On average, half is gone in about four to five hours.
Finally, your kidneys filter the leftovers into your urine.
Only about two to three percent leaves unchanged.
